findings.target: Inherited hard gates and short-circuit precedence
findings.statement: Resolved: comparative adjudication emits all six inherited hard gates, requires exact nonempty and duplicate-free coverage of every configured candidate, and evaluates STALE and failed mandatory gates before insufficiency or semantic Judges.
findings.counterexample: An empty, partial, duplicate, or unexpected candidate-arm set makes candidate_coverage_complete false and therefore fails every inherited comparative gate; a mandatory-gate failure cannot be averaged away by semantic Judges.
findings.pass_condition: Empty, missing, partial, duplicate, or unexpected candidate coverage fails closed; the six inherited gate names remain exact; STALE precedes hard-gate rejection, which precedes insufficiency and semantic adjudication.

findings.target: Closed evidence inventory, frozen inputs, and evidence identities
findings.statement: Resolved: the freeze binds a closed inventory and count, parsed and raw config/policy hashes, rule/schema and implementation groups, hard-gate inputs, and transport evidence; sufficiency rejects duplicate arm/case/run identities.
findings.counterexample: Adding an otherwise valid evidence file changes the live inventory and is rejected even if all previously frozen files retain their hashes; duplicating an arm/case/run identity raises DUPLICATE_EVIDENCE_ID.
findings.pass_condition: Any added, removed, or mutated tracked evidence file, any bound raw or resolved input change, or any duplicate evidence identity is deterministically rejected before adjudication.

findings.statement: Resolved: invalid freeze verification returns a formal STALE action with semantic Judges BLOCKED, ranking PROHIBITED, and no next phase, before any check-mode write or comparison against prior sufficiency and pre-adjudication artifacts.
findings.counterexample: Mutating a frozen dependency while old evidence_sufficiency.json and pre_adjudication_record.json remain present returns STALE instead of reusing or overwriting those older conclusions.
findings.pass_condition: A broken freeze produces STALE, BLOCKED semantic Judges, PROHIBITED ranking, and no route while leaving prior evidence artifacts untouched.

findings.statement: Resolved: report lifecycle wording is derived from route.phase002d_started, while the Phase 002C outcome narrative is derived from pre.short_circuit, pre.decision, and pre.semantic_judges_status rather than hardcoded execution claims.
findings.counterexample: Changing phase002d_started toggles the expansion report between Draft; Not Executed and Execution Recorded; changing the pre-adjudication short-circuit tuple changes the dossier outcome narrative.
findings.pass_condition: Rendered lifecycle and outcome prose changes solely with the authoritative route and pre-adjudication machine inputs and contains no stale hardcoded execution claim.

findings.statement: Missing fields, UNKNOWN values, unrecognized licenses, nonverified review status, and nonliteral runtime booleans now fail closed; however answer_leakage_risk and integration_conflict_risk still accept every unrecognized string beginning with LOW, so the direct-adoption gate map can falsely report all gates passed.
findings.counterexample: With license_status MIT, answer_leakage_risk LOW_UNRECOGNIZED, integration_conflict_risk LOW_UNRECOGNIZED, state_management NONE, one nonempty skill name, empty dangerous/network lists, review_status FULL_RUNTIME_VERIFIED, and both runtime facts literally true, every gate evaluates true although two risk values are not recognized statuses.
findings.pass_condition: Leakage and integration gates accept only explicitly enumerated safe statuses; missing, UNKNOWN, malformed, or arbitrary LOW-prefixed values fail, while the known-safe fixture continues to pass all direct-adoption gates.

findings.statement: Resolved: every Phase 002C automated decision obtains created_at through decision_created_at, which returns the resolved governing policy frozen_at instead of wall-clock time or a mutable config timestamp.
findings.counterexample: Changing runtime time or unrelated configuration cannot change decision created_at; changing the governing frozen policy timestamp changes all derived decision timestamps together.
findings.pass_condition: Every decision created through the shared record path has created_at exactly equal to resolve_policy(root)[frozen_at], independent of wall-clock and unrelated config values.

findings.statement: Resolved: decision_sets_equal builds identity maps only from nonempty string IDs, rejects duplicates and empty sets, and compares complete dictionaries, making equality order-independent while preserving missing-decision and content differences.
findings.counterexample: Reversing an identical nonempty decision list still compares equal; deleting a decision, mutating any payload under the same ID, passing two empty lists, or using an empty or nonstring ID compares unequal.
findings.pass_condition: Only identical nonempty sets of valid uniquely identified decisions compare equal, regardless of file order; missing, changed, empty, or invalid-ID sets fail.

findings.statement: Resolved: either input containing a repeated decision_id returns an invalid identity map, so duplicates cannot be silently collapsed into a passing replay comparison.
findings.counterexample: Two recorded decisions sharing one decision_id compare unequal even if the duplicate content matches the rebuilt decision.
findings.pass_condition: Any duplicate decision_id on either side fails comparison before equality is evaluated.

findings.statement: Resolved for this role: the allowed references now expose the same final-replay implementation whose hash is bound in the current input freeze, permitting independent semantic inspection instead of hash-only trust.
findings.counterexample: A bundle that exposes only the replay hash but not the implementation prevents reviewers from testing identity-collapse counterexamples.
findings.pass_condition: Every first-round role bundle permits reading the exact final-replay implementation bound by the current freeze.
